structure.title: An unsettled succession
structure.text: Illness and continuing rebellion surround a king whose son must prepare for a different kind of authority.

structure.title: Old company, new expectations
structure.text: Falstaff's travels and the court's concerns run alongside one another, measuring what the approaching change means at different social levels.

context.title: A continuing story
context.text: Hal has lived among tavern companions while also serving the crown. This play revisits the obligations created by those different associations.
context.takeaway: The friendships carry an earlier history.

context.title: Recruiting soldiers
context.text: Military needs pass through local officials and personal interests. National purposes can become opportunities for private gain.
context.takeaway: Watch how authority operates away from court.

notice.why: Public roles are performed by people with limited strength.

notice.text: Compare what friends expect from Hal.
notice.why: The same relationship can mean different things to each participant.

opening: The king is ill, rebellion is unfinished, and Prince Hal's old companions still hope his accession will improve their fortunes. Falstaff moves through taverns and recruiting grounds, turning other people's needs into opportunities and refusing to imagine a future without his place beside the prince. Shakespeare follows the approach of a change in government through ageing bodies, unpaid bills, and friendships that mean different things to each participant. Becoming king will require Hal to decide which parts of his former life the crown can accommodate.
